transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Um, I came in because I just feel worn out almost every day. Like, even after a full night's sleep, my body and my head are still dragging when I get up for my cashier shift. I work over at the grocery store, and man, they just changed our store layout again. It's like the third time this year. They moved all the bread all the way to the back past the dairy, and customers keep coming up to my register asking where the bread is. Like I'm supposed to know why corporate wants to hide the bagels, you know? I had this one guy get actually mad at me about it on Tuesday, holding up the whole line just complaining about the buns. But yeah... I don't know, I just wake up and I'm already exhausted before I even clock in.
Do you feel sad or down most of the time?

Sad? No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. Just... worn out, you know? Like I'm not crying or feeling down in the dumps or anything like that. It's funny you mention it though, because this lady at the store yesterday actually asked me if I was sad just because I wasn't smiling enough while I was bagging her groceries. She had this massive cart full of canned cat food—like, an unbelievable amount of cat food. I didn't even know we stocked that many cans of the salmon pate. It made me wonder how many cats she actually has at home. My buddy Dave has three cats and his apartment always smells like ammonia, no matter how much he cleans the litter boxes. I keep telling him he needs to get one of those HEPA air purifiers. I actually saw a pretty decent one on clearance in aisle 4 last week, marked down by like thirty percent... but, um, anyway. What was I saying? Oh, right. No, I don't really feel sad most of the time. Just tired.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next, you know? Like, I'm worrying about money, and then I'm stressing about my wife's brother who's staying in our spare room right now. He was only supposed to be there for a week, but it's been a month, and he eats all my cereal. The good stuff, too, the honey nut kind. I had to hide a box in the trunk of my car just so I'd have breakfast. But anyway, yeah, I worry about him, and my wife is stressed about it, which makes me stressed. And then there's all my church duties, making sure I'm doing enough there, and then I start panicking about whether I'm messing up at work. Like, what if I scan a cucumber as a zucchini? They look so similar, especially when the produce stickers fall off. I found a sticker stuck to the bottom of my shoe the other day, actually. Code 4062. But yeah, my brain just kind of spins like that all the time.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or tasks because they make you feel anxious?

Avoid things? Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work and church and everything. I don't hide in my house or anything like that. Though, man, sometimes I wish I could hide in my house, especially when it's raining. We had this huge thunderstorm on Thursday, and the roof over the loading dock at work started leaking again. It was just pouring right onto the pallets of toilet paper. I told my manager, Rick, about it, but he was too busy trying to fix the self-checkout machine. Those things are always breaking. People try to scan a barcode that's all crumpled up, and the machine just freezes and starts flashing that yellow light. And then I have to walk over there and type in my override code. It's 7-7-2-4, if you were wondering. I picked it because it spells out 'SPUD' on the keypad. I like potatoes. My wife makes this really good potato salad with the red potatoes and a little bit of dill. She usually makes it for the church potluck, which is actually coming up next weekend... but, uh, what did you ask me? Oh, right, avoiding things. No, I don't think I avoid stuff. I just do what I gotta do, even if my head is spinning the whole time.
Do you ever feel like you're not really present or connected to what's happening around you?

Not present? Um, I don't know about not present, but I definitely zone out. Like, I'll be right there at the register, looking dead at the screen, and I just completely lose track of what I'm doing. My brain is just off somewhere else, worrying about the electric bill or if my brother-in-law ate the last of my hidden cereal. And then I realize I haven't scanned the next item, or worse, I have to recount the whole drawer because I lost my place giving change. It's so embarrassing when the customer is just staring at you. This one guy last Tuesday, he was buying like, twelve packs of those little AA batteries. The Energizer ones, not the store brand. The store brand ones are terrible, they die in like a week. I put them in my TV remote once and I was back to getting up to change the channel before the month was out. I actually still have that old tube TV in the basement, it weighs a ton. But yeah, the guy with the batteries was just tapping his card on the counter while I was trying to figure out if I'd already handed him his five dollars back. So, yeah, I guess I do disconnect a bit, just because I can't keep my mind on what's right in front of me.
Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body?

Outside my body? No, I don't think I've ever felt like that. That sounds kind of like a movie, you know? Like one of those sci-fi ones where the guy gets abducted or something. I used to watch a lot of those with my dad when I was a kid. We had this big collection of VHS tapes in the living room, all neatly labeled. He used a label maker for everything. Even the toaster had a little sticker on it that said 'Toaster.' I bought a label maker a few years ago, actually, thinking I'd organize the garage, but I ran out of tape after I did the toolbox and I never bought a refill. The refills are surprisingly expensive, like twelve bucks a pop at the office supply store. I went in there looking for pens the other day—the good gel ones, not the cheap ballpoints that skip—and I saw the label tape and just thought, nope, not paying that. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being outside my body. No, I'm definitely always in my body. Just... my brain is usually somewhere else.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or fog?

A daze? Um, I'm not really sure what you mean by that. Like a fog? I don't know, maybe? I guess sometimes when I'm really tired, but not really a fog. Speaking of fog, though, driving to work on Tuesday was crazy. The fog was so thick you couldn't see the car in front of you. I had to take the back roads because the highway was just a parking lot. I usually take Route 9, but there's this one pothole right near the diner that I always forget about until I hit it. It rattles my whole teeth, I swear. I need to get my alignment checked anyway, the car pulls to the right a little bit. My buddy Dave said he knows a guy who does it cheap, but Dave also told me to invest in this crypto thing last year and I lost fifty bucks, so I don't know if I trust his recommendations anymore. He's a good guy, though, he helped me move my couch when we got the new one. It's one of those sectionals with the cupholders? Really comfortable. But, uh, wait, what did you ask me? A daze? No, I don't think I walk around in a daze. Just regular tired, you know?
Do you often find yourself falling asleep during the day, even when you're not trying to?

Falling asleep during the day? No, I don't really do that. I mean, I'm pretty tired a lot, but I'm not just nodding off at the register or anything. Although, my manager, Gary, he caught this one guy sleeping in the breakroom last month. Just fully laid out on the little faux-leather sofa we have back there. It's not even a comfortable sofa, the springs are all shot on the left side, so you kind of sink into a hole if you sit there. I usually just sit in the plastic chairs at the table when I take my lunch. I bring my own lunch most days—usually just a turkey sandwich, maybe some chips. The vending machine in there is a rip-off anyway, it's like two dollars for a bag of pretzels. And half the time the coils get stuck and your snack just hangs there, taunting you. I tried shaking the machine once and Gary yelled at me, said I was going to break the glass. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sleeping. No, I don't fall asleep during the day. I just stay awake and worry about stuff, mostly.
Is your tiredness usually the first thing you notice in the morning, before you even start your daily activities?

Yeah, pretty much. That's actually why I came in, to be honest. I just feel worn out almost every day. Like, even if I get a full night's sleep, I wake up and my body and my head are just dragging before I even head out for my cashier shift. It's tough because the morning shift at the store gets so busy. We get the whole rush of people buying their morning coffee and scratch-offs. There's this one regular, an older guy who always buys exactly three of the cross-word scratchers. He uses a special silver coin to scratch them, says it's his lucky quarter from 1964 or something. I don't know much about coins, but my uncle used to collect them. He had these big binders full of pennies and dimes, all sorted by year. He tried to get me into it when I was a teenager, but I just didn't have the patience to look at tiny dates on coins for hours. Plus, they smell kind of metallic, you know? Like after you hold a bunch of change your hands smell weird all day. I always wash my hands right after I empty my till at the end of the shift. The soap in the employee bathroom smells like fake green apples, it's really strong. But yeah, what did you ask me? Morning tiredness? Yeah, it's definitely the first thing I feel. Just totally dragging from the second I wake up.
Do you often need to take naps during the day to feel rested?

Naps? Nah, I don't really take naps. Even on my days off, I just can't seem to fall asleep in the middle of the day. Plus, it's way too loud in my apartment building anyway. The guy above me, I swear he's bowling up there or something. He's always dropping heavy stuff right around two or three in the afternoon. I went up there once to ask him to keep it down, and he had this massive fish tank taking up half his living room. Like, huge. It had all these neon rocks at the bottom and a little plastic bubbling pirate ship. I always wanted a fish tank when I was a kid, but my mom said they were too much work to clean. She was probably right, honestly. You have to get the water balance right and clean the filters, and if the power goes out, the fish could freeze. We lost power for three days during that ice storm a couple years ago, remember that? I had to throw out everything in my fridge. Wasted like fifty bucks worth of groceries. The worst was this big block of sharp cheddar cheese I had just bought. I love making grilled cheese with the thick-cut bread from the bakery down the street. They do this sourdough that's amazing. But wait... what were you asking? Oh, taking naps. Yeah, no, I don't nap. I just kind of power through the day, even if I'm dragging.
Is your tiredness more of a physical feeling, like your body is heavy or weak, or is it more of a mental feeling, like you're not focused or can't think clearly?

Honestly, it's kind of both. My body definitely feels heavy, like my arms and legs just weigh a ton when I'm standing behind the register. But my head feels foggy, too. Just... clouded, I guess? It makes it hard to focus on the customers sometimes. Which is bad, because you really have to pay attention when you're counting back change. People get so mad if you short them even a penny. This one lady last week, she bought a pack of gum and handed me a twenty, and I accidentally gave her a five instead of a ten back. She completely snapped at me. Started yelling about how I was trying to scam her. Like, lady, it's a pack of peppermint gum, I'm not running a criminal enterprise here. She had this tiny little dog in her purse, too. One of those Chihuahuas that just shakes constantly. I don't get why people bring dogs into the store, honestly. It's a grocery store, not a park. And the dog was wearing a little pink sweater, which I guess was cute, but it still seems unsanitary. My buddy Mike has a dog, a Golden Retriever, and that thing sheds everywhere. You can't even sit on his couch without getting covered in blonde hair. He has to vacuum like twice a day. I told him he should get one of those robot vacuums, but he said his dog would just bark at it. But anyway, yeah, what was I saying? Oh, right, the tiredness. Yeah, it's my body feeling heavy, but also my brain just feeling totally fuzzy. It's just a lot to deal with.
Does your tiredness stay with you throughout the day or does it get better or worse at certain times?

It pretty much stays with me all day. Like I said earlier, that's really why I made the appointment, because I just feel worn out almost every day. Even if I get a solid eight hours, I wake up and my body and head are just dragging before I even start my cashier shift, and it just kind of hangs on. It's like I never really wake up, you know? Speaking of waking up, my alarm clock broke last week. It was this old digital one I've had since high school, with those big red numbers. I dropped it when I was trying to hit snooze, and the screen just cracked right down the middle. So I've been using my phone, but I hate using my phone for an alarm because then the first thing I see is all my notifications. I get all these emails from stores I bought one thing from like five years ago. Like, I bought a pair of boots online once, and now they email me every single day about their sales. Who buys boots that often? They were good boots, though. Waterproof. I wore them when I went camping with my cousins up by the lake last summer. The mosquitoes were awful up there, just swarming everywhere. We had to buy that heavy-duty bug spray with DEET in it. It smells terrible, kind of like chemicals and old plastic, and it makes your skin feel all sticky. But anyway, what was the question? Oh, if the tiredness changes during the day. Yeah, no, it's pretty much a constant dragging feeling from the minute I wake up until I go back to sleep.
Do you find that your tiredness gets worse when you have to concentrate or think a lot?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really noticed if it gets worse when I have to think a lot. I mean, I guess I try to read sometimes, to like, force my brain to focus on something else besides the register? I picked up this old sci-fi paperback at the thrift store last week. It was only like fifty cents. That thrift store over on Elm Street is great, they have tons of random stuff. I actually found a really nice denim jacket there a while back. It fit perfectly, except the left sleeve was a little frayed at the cuff. I tried to sew it up myself, but man, I am terrible with a needle and thread. I ended up just poking my finger like three times. It bled on the denim, which I guess kind of blends in, but still. My grandma used to make all her own clothes. She had one of those heavy metal sewing machines with the foot pedal, you know the ones? They weigh a ton. We had to move it when she downsized to an apartment, and my cousin threw his back out lifting it. He was out of work for a month, just laying on a heating pad watching daytime TV. He said The Price is Right is still pretty good, but it's not the same without Bob Barker. But um... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my cousin? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I don't really know if thinking hard makes the tiredness worse. I'm just sort of always at that same level of worn out.
Do you feel more tired after you've been doing something that requires a lot of mental work, like balancing your checkbook or trying to solve a puzzle?

I mean, I don't really do puzzles or balance a checkbook. Who balances a checkbook anymore, right? I just check my banking app on my phone. Though honestly, that app is so glitchy sometimes. Last week it said I had negative forty dollars, and I completely panicked. I called the bank, and I was on hold for like forty-five minutes. They play that really smooth jazz music while you wait, but it's super distorted, like it's being played through a tin can. It reminded me of this elevator I got stuck in once at the mall. The doors just wouldn't open, and I was in there with this guy who was carrying a giant pretzel. It smelled amazing, and I was so hungry. We were in there for an hour before they got us out. The mall security guard looked so bored, like it happens every day. But um, yeah, what was I saying? Oh, mental work. I don't really notice if doing stuff like that makes me more tired. I just feel the same amount of tired all the time, no matter what I'm doing.
Are you having trouble completing your daily tasks at work or at home because of your tiredness?

Well, yeah, I guess it is. Like at work, I've had to double-check my cash drawer a lot more often lately because I keep catching myself making these small mistakes. And I've actually had to cut back on volunteering at the food pantry, too, just because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything. It's a shame because I really like helping out there. Although, you wouldn't believe the stuff people donate sometimes. Last week we got a whole cardboard box full of canned oysters. Who eats canned oysters? The labels looked like they were from the nineties, too, all faded and dusty. 

It reminded me of my granddad's basement. He had shelves and shelves of canned food down there because he was convinced the power grid was gonna go down for good one winter. He even bought this massive generator that ran on diesel. He used to start it up once a month just to make sure it worked, and it was so loud you couldn't even hear yourself think. The whole neighborhood probably hated it. He lived next to this lady who had like six outdoor cats, and every time that generator kicked on, you'd just see cats scattering everywhere into the bushes. I'm more of a dog person myself, honestly. I've been thinking about getting a pug, maybe? But um... wait, did you ask about my granddad? Oh, my daily tasks. Right. Yeah, I'm just having a hard time keeping up with the register and the pantry because I'm so drained all the time.
Do you find that being tired makes you less motivated to do things?

I don't know if it's motivation, exactly. I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed if I'm less motivated. I just feel tired. But speaking of motivation, I saw this guy on YouTube the other day who was talking about how to get motivated, and he said you have to take a freezing cold shower every morning at like 4 AM. Who does that? I can barely get myself to take a regular shower some days. My water heater has been acting up anyway, so half the time the water's lukewarm at best. It's this old tank from like 2005. The plumber said I need to replace it, but he quoted me like eight hundred dollars. Eight hundred! I could buy a really decent used car for that back in the day. My first car was this beat-up Honda Civic. It had a tape deck and everything. I used to listen to those old mixtapes my brother made me. He was really into grunge music. He actually plays guitar in a cover band now, they play at this dive bar downtown on Thursday nights. They're not bad, but the sound system there is terrible. But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, motivation. Yeah, I don't think the tiredness really changes my motivation, I just don't have the energy to do the things I want to do.
Do you feel like your tiredness is making you more irritable or emotional than usual?

I don't think so? I mean, I haven't really noticed being more snappy or anything like that. I just feel wiped out. But speaking of being emotional, my sister called me crying the other night because she watched that movie, the one with the dog that waits at the train station? Oh man, she was a wreck. She gets really invested in movies, though. Like, when we were kids, we watched E.T. and she wouldn't go in the closet for a month because she thought an alien was hiding in there. We had this huge walk-in closet in our shared room, and my dad had put all these old winter coats in it. They smelled like mothballs. Actually, I hate the smell of mothballs. It always reminds me of this thrift store down the street from my apartment. I go in there sometimes to look for cheap DVDs, but the whole place smells like old dust and mothballs. I found a sealed copy of The Matrix there once for like two bucks, which was pretty sweet. But anyway, yeah, I don't think I'm more irritable or anything. Just really tired.
Are you finding it harder to spend time with family and friends because of how tired you're feeling?

I don't think so, no. I still see my friends and family about as much as I usually do, I guess. I mean, my buddy Mark came over just this past weekend to watch the game. We always get pizza from this place down the street, Luigi's. They make this incredible deep dish, but the guy who runs it is always yelling at his staff. Like, full-on screaming in Italian. It's kind of dinner and a show, you know? Mark thinks it's hilarious. He actually took Italian in high school because he wanted to study abroad in Rome, but he ended up going to community college with me instead. We had this one professor for history who used to fall asleep while we were taking tests. Just straight-up snoring at his desk. We used to see who could drop their pencil the loudest without waking him up. I think Mark won by dropping a textbook once. But wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, seeing people. Yeah, I still hang out with people, I'm just usually yawning the whole time.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy the things you normally do because of your tiredness?

I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing my normal stuff. Like, I was playing this video game last night... well, it's not a new game, I actually picked it up from the bargain bin at the electronics store next to where I work. I'm a cashier at the grocery store in that same strip mall, and man, the parking lot there is an absolute nightmare right now. They're repaving the whole thing, so everyone has to park in the back near the dumpsters. And yesterday, this lady came through my line and complained about the smell of the tar for like, ten solid minutes while I was trying to scan her produce. She bought like fifteen grapefruits. Who eats that much grapefruit? It messes with certain things, you know, my aunt had to stop eating it when she got put on blood pressure pills. She used to put a thick layer of sugar on half a grapefruit every single morning. Anyway, the lady wouldn't stop talking about the tar, and my register's scanner was acting up, so it kept double-scanning her stuff. I had to call the manager over twice to void the extra items with his key, and he was so annoyed. But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. No, I still enjoy my games and everything, I'm just usually pretty sleepy while I'm playing them.
Are there any activities or relationships that you've had to give up or avoid because of your tiredness?

Well, I wouldn't say I've given up completely on things, but... I guess I've had to make some adjustments. Like at work, I'm a cashier, right? And lately, I've been making these dumb little mistakes with the change. So I've had to start double-checking my cash drawer way more often just to be safe. It's so embarrassing when your drawer comes up short at the end of the shift. My manager, Dave, he's a real stickler about that. He actually fired a guy last year for being five dollars short two days in a row. Though, honestly, I think Dave just didn't like him because the guy always parked his motorcycle in the spot closest to the door. It was this really loud Harley, and he'd rev the engine right outside the breakroom window. I always wanted a motorcycle when I was a teenager, but my mom said absolutely not. She was an ER nurse for twenty years, so she saw all the worst-case scenarios. She used to tell me these awful stories at the dinner table, which really ruined spaghetti night, let me tell you. But anyway, yeah, the cash drawer thing. And... oh, I also used to volunteer at the food pantry on weekends, but I've had to cut back on that. I just don't feel like I can keep up with everything right now. The boxes of canned goods are so heavy, and my lower back has been killing me anyway since I bought this cheap mattress off the internet. It came rolled up in a box, which I still don't understand how they do that. But yeah, the volunteering had to take a backseat.

doctor.intent: determine presence of dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like you're not really present or connected to what's happening around you?

target_item.name: Concentration_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: At the register I can be looking right at the screen and still lose track because I'm thinking about home or bills, and that's when I end up having to recount the drawer or catch a small mistake.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling 'not really present or connected,' which relates to losing focus, mind wandering, or difficulty concentrating on the task at hand.

patient.answer: Not present? Um, I don't know about not present, but I definitely zone out. Like, I'll be right there at the register, looking dead at the screen, and I just completely lose track of what I'm doing. My brain is just off somewhere else, worrying about the electric bill or if my brother-in-law ate the last of my hidden cereal. And then I realize I haven't scanned the next item, or worse, I have to recount the whole drawer because I lost my place giving change. It's so embarrassing when the customer is just staring at you. This one guy last Tuesday, he was buying like, twelve packs of those little AA batteries. The Energizer ones, not the store brand. The store brand ones are terrible, they die in like a week. I put them in my TV remote once and I was back to getting up to change the channel before the month was out. I actually still have that old tube TV in the basement, it weighs a ton. But yeah, the guy with the batteries was just tapping his card on the counter while I was trying to figure out if I'd already handed him his five dollars back. So, yeah, I guess I do disconnect a bit, just because I can't keep my mind on what's right in front of me.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depersonalization (feeling like observing oneself from outside the body), which is not covered by any of the symptoms in my profile.

patient.answer: Outside my body? No, I don't think I've ever felt like that. That sounds kind of like a movie, you know? Like one of those sci-fi ones where the guy gets abducted or something. I used to watch a lot of those with my dad when I was a kid. We had this big collection of VHS tapes in the living room, all neatly labeled. He used a label maker for everything. Even the toaster had a little sticker on it that said 'Toaster.' I bought a label maker a few years ago, actually, thinking I'd organize the garage, but I ran out of tape after I did the toolbox and I never bought a refill. The refills are surprisingly expensive, like twelve bucks a pop at the office supply store. I went in there looking for pens the other day—the good gel ones, not the cheap ballpoints that skip—and I saw the label tape and just thought, nope, not paying that. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being outside my body. No, I'm definitely always in my body. Just... my brain is usually somewhere else.

doctor.intent: determine presence of dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or fog?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling in a daze or fog (depersonalization/derealization or dissociation), which is not covered by the patient's symptom profile (Sleep Disturbance, Fatigue, Excessive Anxiety/Worry, Uncontrollable Worry, Concentration Difficulty, Functional Impairment, Duration). patient.answer: A daze? Um, I'm not really sure what you mean by that. Like a fog? I don't know, maybe? I guess sometimes when I'm really tired, but not really a fog. Speaking of fog, though, driving to work on Tuesday was crazy. The fog was so thick you couldn't see the car in front of you. I had to take the back roads because the highway was just a parking lot. I usually take Route 9, but there's this one pothole right near the diner that I always forget about until I hit it. It rattles my whole teeth, I swear. I need to get my alignment checked anyway, the car pulls to the right a little bit. My buddy Dave said he knows a guy who does it cheap, but Dave also told me to invest in this crypto thing last year and I lost fifty bucks, so I don't know if I trust his recommendations anymore. He's a good guy, though, he helped me move my couch when we got the new one. It's one of those sectionals with the cupholders? Really comfortable. But, uh, wait, what did you ask me? A daze? No, I don't think I walk around in a daze. Just regular tired, you know?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences excessive daytime sleepiness
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself falling asleep during the day, even when you're not trying to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about daytime sleepiness or falling asleep during the day (hypersomnia/narcolepsy symptoms). patient.answer: Falling asleep during the day? No, I don't really do that. I mean, I'm pretty tired a lot, but I'm not just nodding off at the register or anything. Although, my manager, Gary, he caught this one guy sleeping in the breakroom last month. Just fully laid out on the little faux-leather sofa we have back there. It's not even a comfortable sofa, the springs are all shot on the left side, so you kind of sink into a hole if you sit there. I usually just sit in the plastic chairs at the table when I take my lunch. I bring my own lunch most days—usually just a turkey sandwich, maybe some chips. The vending machine in there is a rip-off anyway, it's like two dollars for a bag of pretzels. And half the time the coils get stuck and your snack just hangs there, taunting you. I tried shaking the machine once and Gary yelled at me, said I was going to break the glass. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sleeping. No, I don't fall asleep during the day. I just stay awake and worry about stuff, mostly.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences fatigue as a primary symptom
doctor.question: Is your tiredness usually the first thing you notice in the morning, before you even start your daily activities?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel worn out almost every day, like even after a full night's sleep my body and head are still dragging when I get up for my cashier shift.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking about tiredness in the morning before starting daily activities, which directly relates to the symptom of fatigue.

patient.answer: Yeah, pretty much. That's actually why I came in, to be honest. I just feel worn out almost every day. Like, even if I get a full night's sleep, I wake up and my body and my head are just dragging before I even head out for my cashier shift. It's tough because the morning shift at the store gets so busy. We get the whole rush of people buying their morning coffee and scratch-offs. There's this one regular, an older guy who always buys exactly three of the cross-word scratchers. He uses a special silver coin to scratch them, says it's his lucky quarter from 1964 or something. I don't know much about coins, but my uncle used to collect them. He had these big binders full of pennies and dimes, all sorted by year. He tried to get me into it when I was a teenager, but I just didn't have the patience to look at tiny dates on coins for hours. Plus, they smell kind of metallic, you know? Like after you hold a bunch of change your hands smell weird all day. I always wash my hands right after I empty my till at the end of the shift. The soap in the employee bathroom smells like fake green apples, it's really strong. But yeah, what did you ask me? Morning tiredness? Yeah, it's definitely the first thing I feel. Just totally dragging from the second I wake up.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of hypersomnia
doctor.question: Do you often need to take naps during the day to feel rested?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the need to take naps during the day. My symptom profile does not contain an item specifically about daytime napping or hypersomnolence (only Fatigue and Sleep Disturbance/insomnia). Therefore, none of the profile items directly match the question.

patient.answer: Naps? Nah, I don't really take naps. Even on my days off, I just can't seem to fall asleep in the middle of the day. Plus, it's way too loud in my apartment building anyway. The guy above me, I swear he's bowling up there or something. He's always dropping heavy stuff right around two or three in the afternoon. I went up there once to ask him to keep it down, and he had this massive fish tank taking up half his living room. Like, huge. It had all these neon rocks at the bottom and a little plastic bubbling pirate ship. I always wanted a fish tank when I was a kid, but my mom said they were too much work to clean. She was probably right, honestly. You have to get the water balance right and clean the filters, and if the power goes out, the fish could freeze. We lost power for three days during that ice storm a couple years ago, remember that? I had to throw out everything in my fridge. Wasted like fifty bucks worth of groceries. The worst was this big block of sharp cheddar cheese I had just bought. I love making grilled cheese with the thick-cut bread from the bakery down the street. They do this sourdough that's amazing. But wait... what were you asking? Oh, taking naps. Yeah, no, I don't nap. I just kind of power through the day, even if I'm dragging.

doctor.intent: determine if patient experiences fatigue as a primary symptom
doctor.question: Is your tiredness more of a physical feeling, like your body is heavy or weak, or is it more of a mental feeling, like you're not focused or can't think clearly?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to differentiate whether the fatigue is primarily physical (body heavy/weak) or mental (lack of focus/clarity), which is a detailed follow-up question about the nature of the fatigue not explicitly covered by the 'Fatigue' or 'Concentration_Difficulty' profiles in this specific manner.

patient.answer: Honestly, it's kind of both. My body definitely feels heavy, like my arms and legs just weigh a ton when I'm standing behind the register. But my head feels foggy, too. Just... clouded, I guess? It makes it hard to focus on the customers sometimes. Which is bad, because you really have to pay attention when you're counting back change. People get so mad if you short them even a penny. This one lady last week, she bought a pack of gum and handed me a twenty, and I accidentally gave her a five instead of a ten back. She completely snapped at me. Started yelling about how I was trying to scam her. Like, lady, it's a pack of peppermint gum, I'm not running a criminal enterprise here. She had this tiny little dog in her purse, too. One of those Chihuahuas that just shakes constantly. I don't get why people bring dogs into the store, honestly. It's a grocery store, not a park. And the dog was wearing a little pink sweater, which I guess was cute, but it still seems unsanitary. My buddy Mike has a dog, a Golden Retriever, and that thing sheds everywhere. You can't even sit on his couch without getting covered in blonde hair. He has to vacuum like twice a day. I told him he should get one of those robot vacuums, but he said his dog would just bark at it. But anyway, yeah, what was I saying? Oh, right, the tiredness. Yeah, it's my body feeling heavy, but also my brain just feeling totally fuzzy. It's just a lot to deal with.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's tiredness is persistent throughout the day
doctor.question: Does your tiredness stay with you throughout the day or does it get better or worse at certain times?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel worn out almost every day, like even after a full night's sleep my body and head are still dragging when I get up for my cashier shift.

patient.answer: It pretty much stays with me all day. Like I said earlier, that's really why I made the appointment, because I just feel worn out almost every day. Even if I get a solid eight hours, I wake up and my body and head are just dragging before I even start my cashier shift, and it just kind of hangs on. It's like I never really wake up, you know? Speaking of waking up, my alarm clock broke last week. It was this old digital one I've had since high school, with those big red numbers. I dropped it when I was trying to hit snooze, and the screen just cracked right down the middle. So I've been using my phone, but I hate using my phone for an alarm because then the first thing I see is all my notifications. I get all these emails from stores I bought one thing from like five years ago. Like, I bought a pair of boots online once, and now they email me every single day about their sales. Who buys boots that often? They were good boots, though. Waterproof. I wore them when I went camping with my cousins up by the lake last summer. The mosquitoes were awful up there, just swarming everywhere. We had to buy that heavy-duty bug spray with DEET in it. It smells terrible, kind of like chemicals and old plastic, and it makes your skin feel all sticky. But anyway, what was the question? Oh, if the tiredness changes during the day. Yeah, no, it's pretty much a constant dragging feeling from the minute I wake up until I go back to sleep.

patient.answer: I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really noticed if it gets worse when I have to think a lot. I mean, I guess I try to read sometimes, to like, force my brain to focus on something else besides the register? I picked up this old sci-fi paperback at the thrift store last week. It was only like fifty cents. That thrift store over on Elm Street is great, they have tons of random stuff. I actually found a really nice denim jacket there a while back. It fit perfectly, except the left sleeve was a little frayed at the cuff. I tried to sew it up myself, but man, I am terrible with a needle and thread. I ended up just poking my finger like three times. It bled on the denim, which I guess kind of blends in, but still. My grandma used to make all her own clothes. She had one of those heavy metal sewing machines with the foot pedal, you know the ones? They weigh a ton. We had to move it when she downsized to an apartment, and my cousin threw his back out lifting it. He was out of work for a month, just laying on a heating pad watching daytime TV. He said The Price is Right is still pretty good, but it's not the same without Bob Barker. But um... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my cousin? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I don't really know if thinking hard makes the tiredness worse. I'm just sort of always at that same level of worn out.

patient.answer: I mean, I don't really do puzzles or balance a checkbook. Who balances a checkbook anymore, right? I just check my banking app on my phone. Though honestly, that app is so glitchy sometimes. Last week it said I had negative forty dollars, and I completely panicked. I called the bank, and I was on hold for like forty-five minutes. They play that really smooth jazz music while you wait, but it's super distorted, like it's being played through a tin can. It reminded me of this elevator I got stuck in once at the mall. The doors just wouldn't open, and I was in there with this guy who was carrying a giant pretzel. It smelled amazing, and I was so hungry. We were in there for an hour before they got us out. The mall security guard looked so bored, like it happens every day. But um, yeah, what was I saying? Oh, mental work. I don't really notice if doing stuff like that makes me more tired. I just feel the same amount of tired all the time, no matter what I'm doing.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, I guess it is. Like at work, I've had to double-check my cash drawer a lot more often lately because I keep catching myself making these small mistakes. And I've actually had to cut back on volunteering at the food pantry, too, just because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything. It's a shame because I really like helping out there. Although, you wouldn't believe the stuff people donate sometimes. Last week we got a whole cardboard box full of canned oysters. Who eats canned oysters? The labels looked like they were from the nineties, too, all faded and dusty. 

It reminded me of my granddad's basement. He had shelves and shelves of canned food down there because he was convinced the power grid was gonna go down for good one winter. He even bought this massive generator that ran on diesel. He used to start it up once a month just to make sure it worked, and it was so loud you couldn't even hear yourself think. The whole neighborhood probably hated it. He lived next to this lady who had like six outdoor cats, and every time that generator kicked on, you'd just see cats scattering everywhere into the bushes. I'm more of a dog person myself, honestly. I've been thinking about getting a pug, maybe? But um... wait, did you ask about my granddad? Oh, my daily tasks. Right. Yeah, I'm just having a hard time keeping up with the register and the pantry because I'm so drained all the time.

patient.answer: I don't know if it's motivation, exactly. I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed if I'm less motivated. I just feel tired. But speaking of motivation, I saw this guy on YouTube the other day who was talking about how to get motivated, and he said you have to take a freezing cold shower every morning at like 4 AM. Who does that? I can barely get myself to take a regular shower some days. My water heater has been acting up anyway, so half the time the water's lukewarm at best. It's this old tank from like 2005. The plumber said I need to replace it, but he quoted me like eight hundred dollars. Eight hundred! I could buy a really decent used car for that back in the day. My first car was this beat-up Honda Civic. It had a tape deck and everything. I used to listen to those old mixtapes my brother made me. He was really into grunge music. He actually plays guitar in a cover band now, they play at this dive bar downtown on Thursday nights. They're not bad, but the sound system there is terrible. But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, motivation. Yeah, I don't think the tiredness really changes my motivation, I just don't have the energy to do the things I want to do.

She gets really invested in movies, though. Like, when we were kids, we watched E.T. and she wouldn't go in the closet for a month because she thought an alien was hiding in there. It always reminds me of this thrift store down the street from my apartment. I go in there sometimes to look for cheap DVDs, but the whole place smells like old dust and mothballs. I found a sealed copy of The Matrix there once for like two bucks, which was pretty sweet. But anyway, yeah, I don't think I'm more irritable or anything. Just really tired.

Who eats that much grapefruit? It messes with certain things, you know, my aunt had to stop eating it when she got put on blood pressure pills. She used to put a thick layer of sugar on half a grapefruit every single morning. Anyway, the lady wouldn't stop talking about the tar, and my register's scanner was acting up, so it kept double-scanning her stuff. But anyway, yeah, the cash drawer thing. And... oh, I also used to volunteer at the food pantry on weekends, but I've had to cut back on that.
